questions.question: What will be the output of the following pseudocode?
questions.code:
Integer r_sum(Integer x)
    if(x <= 1)
        return 1
    End if
    return x + r_sum(x - 1)
End function r_sum

Integer tot, i
Set tot = 0
for(i = 1 to 3)
    Set tot = tot + r_sum(i)
End for
Print tot
questions.explanation: Loop calls r_sum(i) for i=1..3. The values are summed together resulting in 10.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following pseudocode?
questions.code:
Integer rec_loop(Integer x)
    if(x <= 0)
        return 0
    End if
    Integer s, i
    Set s = 0
    for(i = 1 to x)
        Set s = s + i
    End for
    return s + rec_loop(x - 1)
End function rec_loop

Integer ans
Set ans = rec_loop(4)
Print ans
questions.explanation: rec_loop(4) sums 1..x for each level down to 1. Total sum = 20.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following pseudocode?
questions.code:
Integer power(Integer a, Integer b)
    if(b <= 0)
        return 1
    End if
    return a * power(a, b - 1)
End function power

Integer val
Set val = power(3, 3)
Print val
questions.explanation: power(3, 3) computes 3^3 recursively: 27.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following pseudocode?
questions.code:
Integer solve_gcd(Integer a, Integer b)
    if(b EQUALS 0)
        return a
    End if
    return solve_gcd(b, a mod b)
End function solve_gcd

Integer ans
Set ans = solve_gcd(16, 4)
Print ans
questions.explanation: Classic Euclidean algorithm to find GCD of 16 and 4. GCD is 4.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following pseudocode?
questions.code:
Integer count_set_bits(Integer n)
    if(n <= 0)
        return 0
    End if
    return (n mod 2) + count_set_bits(n / 2)
End function count_set_bits

Integer bits
Set bits = count_set_bits(26)
Print bits
questions.explanation: count_set_bits(26) extracts binary bits by taking mod 2 and integer dividing by 2. The binary representation of 26 is 11010, which has 3 set bits (1s).
